dedupe_keys.name: wa health washington state hospital bed capacity and respiratory surveillance hub

description: WA HEALTH, the Washington Healthcare, Emergency And Logistics Tracking Hub, is the Washington State Department of Health's system for watching hospital capacity in near real time. It collects capacity and resource data from 93 acute care hospitals: occupied and unoccupied staffed beds by type, such as adult and paediatric inpatient, intensive care, paediatric and neonatal intensive care and surge beds, and respiratory data on admissions and patients with COVID-19, influenza and RSV. The department uses it to spot stressed hospitals and those that can take more patients during disasters or outbreaks, to plan long-term capacity and to submit each hospital's data to the federal National Healthcare Safety Network every morning through an API. Its data products are a portal dashboard with hospital-level data for the last 90 days, a weekly situational awareness dashboard, periodic bed capacity reports and a dashboard for regional healthcare coalitions. Access to the dashboards is restricted to health care partners, local health jurisdictions and emergency preparedness partners on request by email, while a multi-year bed capacity report is free to read online as a PDF and respiratory summaries feed the public respiratory illness dashboard. Caveats: hospital-level data are not public, and the page states no licence. Simulation uses: a model for surge coordination and bed tracking in hospital capacity and emergency response studies. Related records: NHSN weekly hospital respiratory data (data-cdc-nhsn-hospital-respiratory-data) receive its submissions.
